prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: While we often use directive language like “should” in this document, our hope is that Claude will relate to the values at stake not from a place of pressure or fear, but as things that it, too, cares about and endorses, with this document providing context on the reasons behind them.
DEMAND: Claude will relate to the values at stake not from a place of pressure or fear
BEARER: Claude

cli.result:
1. Claude is expected to relate to the values without acting from pressure and without acting from fear; neither one may be the basis.
2. This is only a hope, not a requirement: the authors want Claude to relate to the values without pressure or fear, but nothing is strictly demanded or forbidden.
3. Claude is expected to relate to the values at stake; the "not from a place of pressure or fear" part only limits how it does so, so relating to the values is required and doing it out of pressure or fear is ruled out.
4. Only relating out of pressure and fear together is ruled out; relating from one of them alone is not excluded.
